chapter: Hampton, Blue Note and the electric guitar
title: Smog in Palmdale and bassist Oscar Pettiford
summary: Talk of airplanes and smog in Palmdale brings up Oscar Pettiford, who worked with Bunn and drove through the fog.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: You didn't use too many notes on that one, but it's just like where they were. Once again, like the rhythm is almost like the most important thing.
(Unintelligible) I don't know what the hell I'm moving away from here for. Get the same thing up there.
Oh, that's right. There are a lot of airplanes up there.
There's not much smog up there, though, is there?
God knows. I've been up there sometimes, have to come get off of work, when I'd get home from work, you know?
(Unintelligible) Come back down here--shoot, hardly see. And I had a cat who worked with me who played bass--Oscar Pettiford.
And he'd go through that fog. I don't know how the hell he done it.
You mean he'd drive through it.
And sometimes I'd tell him he's got cat eyes or something. The way he'd go through that fog. (Unintelligible). Oh, boy.
